title: Foreground, Background, Backdrop
caption: Telescopes under the Milky Way, Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way fills the sky behind a group of telescopes at NSF NOIRLab's Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO). The Thai Southern Hemisphere Telescope stands in the foreground, and five of the seven PROMPT telescopes are clustered behind it. With our home galaxy as a backdrop, the telescopes are easy to overlook.

The Thai telescope is part of the Thai Robotic Telescope Network (TRTN), run by the National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand (NARIT). As its name suggests, the telescope is the network's instrument in the southern hemisphere.

PROMPT stands for Panchromatic Robotic Optical Monitoring and Polarimetry Telescopes. Robotic telescopes can carry out observations without an astronomer at the controls. Panchromatic means working across a wide range of colours, and polarimetry is the measurement of how light waves are oriented, which can reveal details that brightness alone does not.

understand.summary: A night landscape photograph by B. Tafreshi. No camera or exposure details or colour mapping are published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the Milky Way would look fainter to someone standing among these telescopes.
